result.process_description:
Title: LAN Party

You are planning a LAN party for 10 friends, so the first thing you have to do is to send invitations to these 10 friends.
Next, you have to find out which games they want to play.
As soon as you have received a list of games, you can appoint a date when the LAN party is going to happen.
If 8 or more people agree on this date, you are good to continue.
Else, you have to appoint another date, until 8 people are free to join you.
While you find a date, you can find out if you have all the games your guests want to play.
If some are missing, download them.
Next, you should find out how much beer your friends will require.
If you do not have enough, buy what's missing.
After that, you can enjoy the LAN party.

result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.

Do not connect the request task directly to the decision, because the decision cannot be made until the replies have arrived.

When The description says that a step can only continue once other people have responded, for example when it says to continue only after responses have been received, or until a required number of people have replied.: Model an intermediate catch event that waits for those responses, placed after the activity that requests them and before the decision or activity that depends on them. Do not replace the wait with a task or a gateway. Keep the activity that acts on the responses as a separate element after the catch event.

When the description says that after a request is sent, a party may send a reply or message that the process waits for, and it also states a deadline for that reply after which a different consequence follows; the description names the received reply with its own wording, distinct from the deadline: Model the received reply as its own message intermediate catch event, labeled with the reply as the description names it (the verb and object the description uses for receiving it). Model the passing of the deadline as a separate timer intermediate catch event labeled as the deadline, placed on its own branch. Do not label one catch event with the deadline when the description names a received reply for that branch, and do not swap the two labels.

When the description describes a step where the process waits, phrased as an activity (for example 'awaiting' an outcome) and names no message, signal, timer or condition that is received: Model this waiting step as a task in the sequence, placed after the preceding activity and before the next step, with sequence flows connecting it on both sides. Do not replace it with an intermediate catch event, and do not add a flow from the preceding activity directly to the next gateway that skips the task. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description names a specific message, signal, timer or condition to be received.
